title: A depth-one circuit for a single gate over literals
statement: Fix an arity $k$, a gate type given by a flag that selects AND when true and OR when false, and a family of polarities $\sigma : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{F}_2$. For each variable index $j \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, let $\ell_j$ be the literal on variable $j$ with polarity $\sigma(j)$, and let $G$ be the single gate of the chosen type applied to the list $\ell_0, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_{k-1}$. Then there is a Boolean circuit $c'$ of depth at most $1$ that computes the same Boolean function as $G$: for every assignment $g : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{F}_2$, the value of $c'$ at $g$ equals the value of $G$ at $g$.
hypotheses_covered: gate type flag (AND when true, OR when false)
polarity family signs : Fin k → Bool
agreement with the single gate over the k literals on every assignment g
replaced:
For any flag $\mathit{isAnd}$, arity $k$, and sign family $\mathit{signs} : \mathrm{Fin}\,k
\to \mathrm{Bool}$, there is a circuit $c'$ of depth at most $1$ that equals the node
$\mathrm{Circuit.node}\,\mathit{isAnd}$ over the literals $\mathrm{Circuit.lit}\,\langle j,
\mathit{signs}\,j\rangle$, evaluating identically on every input assignment $g$.
